fictionality.statement: Every study, author label, title, abstract, locator, result, search receipt, citation, and date in this fixture was authored for instruction and has no real-world referent.
fictionality.identifier_policy: Records use local fixture IDs only; no DOI, ISBN, trial registration, repository identifier, or journal citation is asserted.

review_protocol.question: In fictional post-secondary study-planning contexts, what evidence in this toy corpus addresses whether an optional AI explanation changes immediate task revision quality?
review_protocol.intervention: an optional AI-generated explanation attached to a study-planning suggestion
review_protocol.comparator: the same suggestion without the explanation
eligible_designs: quasi-experimental comparison with a stated assignment mechanism
qualitative study of participant interpretation when it does not make an effect claim
exclude: duplicate reports of an already included study unless they add a distinct eligible outcome
review_protocol.primary_outcome_window: the first revision completed within 48 fictional hours
review_protocol.analysis_boundary: The fixture supports workflow practice only. No pooled effect or real educational conclusion is authorised.

search_receipts.query: (artificial intelligence OR AI) AND explanation AND (revision OR study planning) AND student

records.title: Optional explanations and first-draft revision in two fictional seminar sections
records.abstract: Two fictional seminar sections were assigned by timetable rather than random allocation. One section received study suggestions with optional explanations and one received suggestions alone. The report describes a small difference in immediate revision scores and names baseline imbalance as a limitation.

full_text_extract.method_text: Section assignment followed the existing timetable; no random allocation was performed.
full_text_extract.result_text: Explanation group: n=28, mean=3.4, SD=0.6; comparison group: n=25, mean=3.1, SD=0.7.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: The groups differed at baseline and the analysis does not identify a causal effect.

records.title: Learners interpreting machine explanations during study-plan revision
records.abstract: A fictional qualitative interview study explores how post-secondary participants interpreted optional AI explanations. It reports uncertainty, perceived usefulness, and reasons for rejecting suggestions, but does not compare revision outcomes.

full_text_extract.method_text: Twelve volunteers who had opened at least one explanation were interviewed using a fictional semi-structured guide.
full_text_extract.result_text: Participants described the explanation as a reason to inspect the suggestion, not as proof that it was correct.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: Volunteer accounts do not establish prevalence, effectiveness, or the experiences of non-users.

records.title: Automated study reminders in fictional secondary schools
records.abstract: A school-age reminder system sends fixed messages. It contains no AI-generated explanation and measures attendance rather than revision quality.

full_text_extract.method_text: The reminders used three fixed templates and did not include generated explanations.
full_text_extract.result_text: The reported outcome was weekly attendance.

records.title: Why explainable tutoring will transform learning
records.abstract: A conceptual commentary argues that explanation is promising. It reports no original participants, assignment, observation, or extractable outcome.

full_text_extract.method_text: This article offers a perspective and reports no empirical study.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: The proposed benefits require empirical evaluation.

records.title: A fictional randomised comparison of explanation access during revision
records.abstract: Fictional participants were randomly assigned to an optional-explanation interface or a suggestion-only interface. The primary outcome and attrition are reported, while no subgroup effect was preregistered.

full_text_extract.method_text: A seeded fictional random-number list allocated 80 participant codes equally before the interface opened.
full_text_extract.result_text: Available cases: explanation n=36, mean=3.6, SD=0.5; comparison n=38, mean=3.3, SD=0.6; mean difference 0.30, fictional 95% interval 0.05 to 0.55.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: Six participant codes lacked the primary outcome; no subgroup effect was preregistered.

records.title: A fictional randomised comparison of explanation access during revision: repository copy
records.abstract: This is an authored duplicate carrier of REC-005 with minor formatting differences and no distinct outcome.

full_text_extract.method_text: The methods describe the same 80 fictional participant codes as REC-005.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: No additional eligible outcome is reported.

records.title: Explanations, revision, and confidence in a fictional open workshop
records.abstract: A one-group workshop measures revision quality before and after learners choose whether to open explanations. The assignment mechanism is not reported and self-selection is unresolved.

full_text_extract.method_text: All participants could open explanations; exposure was not assigned and the report does not list non-openers.
full_text_extract.result_text: The average fictional revision score increased after the workshop.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: The document contains no labelled limitations section.

records.title: Protocol for a fictional explanation-and-revision comparison
records.abstract: A protocol specifies an eligible randomised comparison, but no recruitment, outcome, or result has occurred.

full_text_extract.method_text: The authors plan to randomise 120 fictional participant codes.

records.title: Revision quality after optional explanations: fictional pilot dataset note
records.abstract: A data note describes columns and missing values but does not state an assignment mechanism or provide a study report that can support an effect claim.

full_text_extract.method_text: The note defines revision_score and explanation_opened but omits exposure assignment and recruitment.
full_text_extract.result_text: Nine of 50 fictional rows lack revision_score.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: The table is not an analysis and does not identify an effect.

records.title: Instructor accounts of introducing optional machine explanations
records.abstract: Fictional instructors describe implementation choices. Learner interpretation and revision quality were not observed.

full_text_extract.method_text: Eight fictional instructors joined two focus groups.
full_text_extract.result_text: Instructors described uncertainty about when to show explanations.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: No learner data or revision tasks were collected.

records.title: Correction notice for the fictional Alder seminar report
records.abstract: The correction changes the comparison-group standard deviation in REC-001 from 0.7 to 0.9 and leaves all other authored values unchanged.

full_text_extract.method_text: This notice corrects one fictional table cell.
full_text_extract.result_text: REC-001 comparison-group revision_quality SD should read 0.9, not 0.7.
full_text_extract.limitation_text: No other value or conclusion is changed.

citation_audit_cases.draft_claim: Optional explanations caused a 0.3-point improvement in all post-secondary learners.
citation_audit_cases.problem: The fixture record reports a single fictional sample, missing outcomes, and a bounded mean difference; it cannot support a universal claim.
citation_audit_cases.safer_wording: In one fictional randomised comparison, available-case revision scores were 0.30 points higher in the explanation group; the authored interval was 0.05 to 0.55, and six outcomes were missing.

citation_audit_cases.problem: A 12-volunteer qualitative fixture can support a theme description, not prevalence or a population frequency.
citation_audit_cases.safer_wording: Some fictional volunteers described explanations as prompts to inspect a suggestion rather than as proof of correctness.

citation_audit_cases.draft_claim: The Alder comparison group's SD was 0.7.
citation_audit_cases.problem: REC-011 corrects the cell to 0.9; a locator-only workflow that misses linked corrections produces a stale extraction.
citation_audit_cases.safer_wording: The linked fictional correction sets the comparison-group SD to 0.9.

known_boundaries: This is not a real bibliographic corpus and must not be cited as evidence.
Screening hints are authored answer-checking aids, not labels produced by independent reviewers.
Page, table, section, and paragraph locators point only to fictional text embedded in this JSON file.
The corpus is too small and artificial for a meta-analysis, evidence grade, publication-bias assessment, prevalence statement, causal generalisation, or policy recommendation.
RAG or search may locate a record, but every claim must be checked against the embedded primary text and its stated boundary.
